faq.q: Is January a good month for a boat rental in Marbella?
faq.a: Yes, January offers calm seas and fewer crowds. Average air temperatures are 14–18°C, sea temps 14–16°C. You’ll enjoy peaceful views of La Concha and the Sierra Blanca. Just bring a light jacket and check the wind forecast — Poniente days are best.

faq.q: What is the typical wind in Marbella during January?
faq.a: Dominant winds are Poniente (west, 10–15 knots) and Levante (east, up to 20 knots). Poniente brings stable, milder conditions; Levante can be choppier. Most charters stay within 4 NM of the coast, so even moderate wind is manageable.

faq.q: Which boat do you recommend for a January charter?
faq.a: For a group of up to 9, the Astondoa 40 (€749/2h) or Azimut 39 (€749/2h) are excellent — both have enclosed saloons and flybridge covers. For larger parties, the Mangusta 80 (€4,719/4h) includes a free jet ski and heated cabin space.

faq.q: Can I swim in the sea in January in Marbella?
faq.a: Swimming is possible but bracing — sea temps are 14–16°C. Most guests prefer to enjoy the scenery and stay dry. If you do swim, a wetsuit is recommended. Our boats are equipped with safety gear and life jackets.

faq.q: What are the best destinations for a January cruise from Puerto Banús?
faq.a: Popular short trips include Cala del Faro (2 NM west), Cala Cortés (3 NM east), or a scenic loop past the Golden Mile and Marbella Marina. All are sheltered and offer stunning views of the Costa del Sol.

data.body_html:
January in Marbella brings crisp air, quiet marinas, and surprisingly pleasant cruising conditions. If you're considering a Marbella boat rental in January 2030, this guide covers everything you need: average temperatures, wind patterns, sea state, and insider tips for making the most of a winter charter from Puerto Banús.

Marbella January Weather Overview

January is the coolest month on the Costa del Sol, but 'cool' is relative. Daytime highs average 16–18°C, with overnight lows around 8–10°C. Sea temperatures hover between 14°C and 16°C — too cold for a long swim, but perfect for a scenic cruise with a warm jacket and a glass of cava.

Rainfall is modest: 6–8 days of light showers per month. Most days are sunny or partly cloudy. Sunrise is around 08:30, sunset at 18:30, giving you a solid 10 hours of daylight — ideal for a 2- to 4-hour charter.

Wind & Sea Conditions

Wind in January is dominated by two patterns: Poniente (west wind, 10–15 knots) and Levante (east wind, 15–20 knots). Poniente days are generally calmer and warmer, making them the best choice for a boat rental. Levante can bring choppier seas, especially east of Marbella, but our experienced skippers know the sheltered routes.

Wave height rarely exceeds 1–1.5 metres inside the bay. Most charters stay within 4–6 nautical miles of Puerto Banús, so even moderate winds are manageable. Always check the Marbella boat rental forecast before booking — our team provides real-time updates via WhatsApp.

Recommended Boats for January

For winter cruising, enclosed spaces and heating make a big difference. Our top picks:

  • Astondoa 40 (12.5m, 9 pax) — €749/2h or €2,299/8h. Enclosed saloon, flybridge cover, ideal for small groups.
  • Azimut 39 (12.5m, 11 pax) — same pricing as Astondoa 40. Spacious interior, good for families.
  • Mangusta 80 (24m, 12 pax) — €4,719 minimum 4h, includes a free jet ski. Heated cabin, panoramic views.
  • Azimut 58 Flybridge (17.6m, 12 pax) — pricing on request. Flybridge with full enclosure, perfect for cooler days.

All charters include a licensed skipper, fuel, drinks, snacks, and insurance — no surprises.

Best January Itineraries from Puerto Banús

Short cruises work best in winter. Here are three routes our skippers recommend:

  • Cala del Faro (2 NM west) — sheltered cove with views of the Sierra Blanca. Great for a quiet lunch stop.
  • Cala Cortés (3 NM east) — calm bay near the Golden Mile. Often less windy than open water.
  • Marbella Marina loop (4 NM round trip) — cruise past the port, La Concha mountain, and the luxurious beach clubs. A photographer's dream in the low winter sun.

For longer charters (6–8 hours), you can head to Estepona (8 NM west) or Sotogrande (12 NM west) — but these depend on favourable wind windows.

What to Wear & Bring

Layers are key. A fleece or light down jacket under a windproof shell works well. Sunglasses and sunscreen are still essential — the sun reflects strongly off the water even in January. Non-slip shoes are recommended, especially on wet decks.

Our boats provide water, soft drinks, beer, wine, and snacks. If you want a hot drink, bring a thermos — we'll happily keep it topped up.

Booking Tips for January 2030

January is low season, so availability is good — but we still recommend booking 2–3 days ahead via WhatsApp. This allows us to monitor the forecast and suggest the best day. If conditions turn poor, we offer a full refund or free rescheduling.

For the best value, book a 2-hour charter on a Tier A boat (Astondoa 40 or Azimut 39) at €749. For larger groups, the Mangusta 80 at €4,719 (4h) includes a jet ski — a fun addition even in winter.
